Title: Smartphone-based home care model improved use of cardiac rehabilitation in postmyocardial infarction patients: results from a randomised controlled trial
Author: Varnfield M, Karunanithi M, Lee C-K, et al.
Comment: Timepoint mismatch with synthesis plan: the latest timepoint with extractable arm-level triglyceride mean/SD/n is 6 weeks (~1.5 months), i.e. outside the planned 3-12 month window; the paper's 6-month figure (Figure 4) reports only 6MWT, LDL and HDL, so no 6-month triglyceride mean/SD is stated. M_diff computed as group_2_mean - group_1_mean from the explicitly reported absolute 6-week means (1.13 - 1.05 = 0.08). The paper's own ANCOVA-adjusted mean difference for change was -0.26 (95% CI -0.51 to -0.01, p=0.04) but its sign convention (which arm minus which) is not explicitly stated, so it was not entered as M_diff. Lipid data available for only 46-65% of participants.
domain: cardiac rehabilitation / secondary prevention after myocardial infarction
Study Environment: four community cardiac rehabilitation centres in Brisbane, Australia, and participants' homes
Participant type: post-myocardial-infarction patients referred to cardiac rehabilitation
Recruitment source: Primary & Community Health Services, Metro North Health Service District, Queensland Health, Australia (CR referral lists), 2009-2011
Outcome measurement: Absolute 6-week follow-up arm-level mean±SD (Table 2); between-group ANCOVA adjusted mean difference for baseline-to-6-week change (Table 3)
effect_direction: Home-based (smartphone CAP-CR) mean slightly higher than centre-based at follow-up (1.13 vs 1.05 mmol/L; raw diff +0.08), i.e. numerically favouring centre-based; the paper's baseline-adjusted ANCOVA difference (-0.26) favoured home-based.

Title: Home-Based Aerobic Interval Training Improves Peak Oxygen Uptake Equal to Residential Cardiac Rehabilitation: A Randomized, Controlled Trial
Author: Moholdt et al.
Comment: No between-group ANCOVA CI or p-value was reported for triglycerides (only HDL had a reported significant between-group difference); within-group EMMs were residential 0.24 (-0.25, 0.73) and home AIT -0.12 (-0.67, 0.43). M_diff computed as group_2_mean - group_1_mean (1.4 - 1.6) from explicitly reported follow-up means in a simple two-group between-subjects design. Values already in mmol/L; no unit conversion applied.
Participant type: Patients 4-8 weeks after coronary artery bypass graft surgery, clinically stable
Outcome measurement: Serum triglyceride concentration at 6-month follow-up (absolute follow-up value, mean ± SD)
effect_direction: Home-based aerobic interval training lower than residential centre-based CR at 6 months (1.4 vs 1.6 mmol/L; diff -0.2), favouring home-based; not statistically tested.

Title: Effects and costs of real-time cardiac telerehabilitation: randomised controlled non-inferiority trial
Author: Maddison R, Rawstorn JC, Stewart RAH, et al.
Comment: Values already reported in mmol/L, so no unit conversion applied. Per-outcome analysed Ns are not reported in Tables 2/3; randomised Ns (REMOTE-CR 82, centre-based 80) were used, and attrition was 13.6% at 12 weeks, so actual analysed N is likely lower. M_diff is the paper's ANCOVA-adjusted mean difference (REMOTE-CR minus centre-based), not a raw difference of the tabulated means (raw difference would be -0.18). SE_diff was derived from the reported 95% CI as (0.22 - (-0.34))/3.92 = 0.143; no SE or p-value was reported for this outcome. Triglycerides were measured only at baseline and 12 weeks (no 24-week value), so 12 weeks is the latest eligible follow-up.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('REMOTE-CR (remotely monitored home-based exercise cardiac telerehabilitation)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: cardiac rehabilitation / secondary prevention of coronary heart disease
Study Environment: clinical / community (remote home-based delivery vs cardiac rehabilitation clinics)
Medium: smartphone app plus chest-worn wearable sensor (telerehabilitation platform) vs face-to-face supervised sessions
Content length: 12-week intervention; outcomes at baseline, 12 and 24 weeks
Participant type: Clinically stable adults (>=18 years) with a documented diagnosis of coronary heart disease within 6 months (mean age 61±12.7 years, 86% men)
Recruitment source: Metropolitan hospitals, outpatient clinics and community-based cardiac rehabilitation seminars in Auckland and Tauranga, New Zealand
Outcome measurement: Absolute follow-up values (week 12) reported as mean±SD per arm; adjusted mean difference from ANCOVA adjusted for baseline outcome, age and sex
effect_direction: Home-based telerehabilitation (REMOTE-CR) lower than centre-based at 12 weeks (1.48 vs 1.66 mmol/L; adjusted mean difference -0.06, 95% CI -0.34 to 0.22), favouring home-based but non-significant/comparable.

Title: Program Participation, Exercise Adherence, Cardiovascular Outcomes, and Program Cost of Traditional Versus Modified Cardiac Rehabilitation
Author: Carlson, Johnson, Franklin, VanderLaan
Comment: Between-group comparison for triglycerides reported only narratively as non-significant; no exact between-group p-value, test statistic, or effect size given (the p=0.012 footnote refers to within-group time effects, not the protocol comparison). M_diff computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean (140 − 144) from the two explicitly reported 6-month means in mg/dl (simple two-group between-subjects design); not converted to mmol/L. Per-arm Ns differ from randomized Ns due to attrition (differential dropout, more in TP).
Study Environment: Hospital-based cardiac rehabilitation program plus off-site/home exercise
Participant type: low- to moderate-risk cardiac patients (post-CABG, PTCA, myocardial infarction, or documented CAD), aged 35–75 years
Recruitment source: First-time referrals to a hospital cardiac rehabilitation program, metropolitan hospital, midwestern USA
Outcome measurement: Serum triglyceride concentration, fasting venous blood sample, 6-month follow-up absolute value
effect_direction: Modified (off-site/home-based) protocol slightly lower than traditional centre-based protocol at 6 months (140 vs 144 mg/dL; diff -4 mg/dL ≈ -0.05 mmol/L), favouring home-based; reported as non-significant.

Report_ID: Triglycerides (mg/dl), change from baseline at 12 weeks — physician-supervised, nurse–case-managed (home-based exercise, office + telephone visits) vs contemporary centre-based phase 2 cardiac rehabilitation
Title: Effectiveness of Three Models for Comprehensive Cardiovascular Disease Risk Reduction
Author: Gordon NF, English CD, Contractor AS, Salmon RD, Leighton RF, Franklin BA, Haskell WL
Comment: Paper reports change-from-baseline only (no absolute 12-week means). No arm-specific p-value or test statistic reported for triglycerides; only a narrative statement of no significant difference among the 3 interventions. M_diff computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean from the two explicitly reported change means (simple two-arm contrast within a 3-arm parallel RCT). Values in mg/dl; conversion factor to mmol/L supplied. Shared centre-based control arm (n=45) is also used for the community-based comparison row (correlated effects).
domain: cardiac rehabilitation / secondary prevention of coronary artery disease
Study Environment: clinical (hospital cardiac rehabilitation, physician office, community retail/mall sites) with home-based exercise
Participant type: Low- or moderate-risk adults (aged 21–75) with documented coronary artery disease
Recruitment source: St. Joseph's/Candler Health System and community sites, Savannah, Georgia
Outcome measurement: Mean ± SD change from baseline in fasting serum triglycerides (mg/dl), all patients, Table 2
Outcome variable: Triglycerides (mg/dl), change from baseline at 12 weeks — physician-supervised, nurse–case-managed (home-based exercise, office + telephone visits) vs contemporary centre-based phase 2 cardiac rehabilitation
effect_direction: Home-based nurse–case-managed arm showed a small rise (+2.5 mg/dL) vs a fall in centre-based CR (-12.7 mg/dL); difference +15.2 mg/dL (≈ +0.17 mmol/L) favours centre-based; reported as non-significant.
